tools.name: -health-check
tools.description: Internal health check tool. Verifies GitHub OAuth credentials and connectivity.

tools.name: list-repos
tools.description: List repositories accessible to the current user via the Teros GitHub App (across every installation reachable). Pass `owner` to filter to a specific user/org.

owner.description: Optional filter — only return repos under this user or organization.

tools.name: get-repo
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific repository

tools.name: create-repo
tools.description: Create a new repository

org.description: Organization name. If provided, creates repo under the org.

tools.name: list-issues
tools.description: List issues for a repository with optional filters

tools.name: get-issue
tools.description: Get details of a specific issue

tools.name: create-issue
tools.description: Create a new issue in a repository

assignees.description: Array of GitHub usernames to assign

tools.name: update-issue
tools.description: Update an existing issue. Setting `state: "closed"` closes it (use `state_reason` for completed/not_planned). `labels` REPLACES the entire label set — use add-labels-to-issue to append.

tools.name: add-issue-comment
tools.description: Add a comment to an issue

tools.name: add-labels-to-issue
tools.description: Add labels to an issue or pull request (PRs are issues in the API). Returns the full label set after the addition.

labels.description: Label names to add (case sensitive). Existing labels are preserved.

tools.name: search-issues
tools.description: Search issues and pull requests across GitHub. Use GitHub search syntax in `q` (e.g. `repo:owner/name is:issue is:open label:bug`). Returns {total_count, incomplete_results, items[]}.

q.description: Search query (GitHub search syntax). Supports qualifiers like `repo:`, `is:`, `label:`, `author:`, `assignee:`.

tools.name: list-pulls
tools.description: List pull requests for a repository

tools.name: get-pull
tools.description: Get details of a specific pull request

tools.name: create-pull
tools.description: Create a new pull request

base.description: Branch name to merge into (default: main)

tools.name: merge-pull
tools.description: Merge a pull request

tools.name: list-pr-files
tools.description: List files changed in a pull request. Each file includes {filename, status, additions, deletions, changes, patch?, sha, blob_url}.

tools.name: list-pr-commits
tools.description: List commits on a pull request. Each commit includes {sha, commit.message, author, html_url}.

tools.name: list-pr-review-comments
tools.description: List review comments (inline comments on diff) of a pull request. Returns array with {id, user, body, path, line, commit_id, created_at}.

tools.name: request-reviewers
tools.description: Request reviewers on a pull request. Returns the PR with `requested_reviewers` and `requested_teams` populated.

reviewers.description: GitHub usernames to request review from

team_reviewers.description: Team slugs (within the org) to request review from

tools.name: create-pr-review
tools.description: Create a pull request review. `event` controls the verdict: APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / COMMENT. Returns review {id, state, user, submitted_at}.

body.description: Review body (markdown). Required for REQUEST_CHANGES and COMMENT, optional for APPROVE.

commit_id.description: SHA of the commit the review applies to (default: latest of the PR)

comments.description: Inline comments. Each item: {path, position OR line, body}.

tools.name: list-branches
tools.description: List branches in a repository

tools.name: get-branch
tools.description: Get information about a specific branch

tools.name: create-branch
tools.description: Create a new branch from a reference

tools.name: list-commits
tools.description: List commits in a repository

sha.description: SHA or branch name to list commits from

tools.name: get-commit
tools.description: Get details of a specific commit

tools.name: compare-commits
tools.description: Compare two commits or branches. `basehead` format `BASE...HEAD` (e.g. `main...feat/x`). Returns {status, ahead_by, behind_by, total_commits, commits[], files[].patch}.

basehead.description: Comparison range, format `BASE...HEAD`. May include cross-fork via `owner:ref`.

tools.name: list-workflows
tools.description: List workflows in a repository

tools.name: list-workflow-runs
tools.description: List workflow runs for a repository

tools.name: get-workflow-run
tools.description: Get a workflow run. Returns {id, name, status, conclusion, run_number, head_branch, head_sha, html_url, created_at, updated_at, run_started_at}.

tools.name: list-workflow-run-jobs
tools.description: List jobs of a workflow run. Each job includes {id, name, status, conclusion, started_at, completed_at, html_url, steps[]}.

tools.name: trigger-workflow
tools.description: Trigger a workflow dispatch event

tools.name: rerun-workflow-run
tools.description: Re-run a workflow run. By default re-runs only failed jobs (faster + cheaper). Set `mode: "all"` to re-run every job.

enable_debug_logging.description: Whether to enable debug logging for the re-run (default: false)

tools.name: cancel-workflow-run
tools.description: Cancel a workflow run that is in progress. Returns {success: true} on 202 Accepted.

tools.name: list-releases
tools.description: List releases of a repository, newest first. Each release includes {id, tag_name, name, draft, prerelease, body, html_url, published_at, author}.

tools.name: create-release
tools.description: Create a GitHub release tagged at `tag_name`. If `target_commitish` omitted GitHub uses the default branch. Returns {id, tag_name, name, html_url, draft, prerelease, published_at}.

tag_name.description: Tag this release points to (created if missing)

target_commitish.description: Branch or SHA the tag is created from (default: repository default branch)

generate_release_notes.description: Auto-generate release notes from commits (default: false)

tools.name: get-file-content
tools.description: Get the content of a file in a repository

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit SHA (default: default branch)

tools.name: create-or-update-file
tools.description: Create or update a file in a repo. Pass `sha` of the existing file when updating. Path must not contain `..` or start with `/`.

path.description: File path in repository (no `..`, no leading `/`)

sha.description: SHA of file being replaced (required for updates)

tools.name: search-repos
tools.description: Search for repositories on GitHub

tools.name: search-code
tools.description: Search for code across GitHub repositories

tools.name: get-installation-context
tools.description: List the Teros GitHub App installations reachable by the current user, with accessible repos, granted permissions, and manage/install URLs.

tools.name: get-user
tools.description: List the Teros GitHub App installations reachable by the current user, with accessible repos, granted permissions, and manage/install URLs.

tools.name: create-check-run
tools.description: Create a check run on a commit (exclusive to GitHub Apps). The check appears in the PR/commit sidebar. Use status:in_progress while the check runs, then update with conclusion when done.

name.description: Display name of the check (e.g. "Teros review")

head_sha.description: Commit SHA the check applies to

output.description: Rich output with title, summary (markdown), optional text body

details_url.description: Optional URL with more detail (shown as link in the check)

external_id.description: Reference ID controlled by the App (idempotency on App side)

tools.name: update-check-run
tools.description: Update an existing check run — typically to set status:completed + conclusion when work finishes. Pass only the fields you want to change.

tools.name: get-rate-limit
tools.description: Read the current GitHub API rate-limit budget for the installation token. Returns per-bucket {limit, remaining, reset, used} — core, search, graphql, code_search.

tools.name: dispatch-event
tools.description: Send a `repository_dispatch` event to trigger workflows configured to listen for it. Pass `event_type` (string the workflow filters on) and optional `client_payload`.

event_type.description: Custom event type the workflow filters on (e.g. `deploy-staging`)

client_payload.description: Optional payload (max 10 properties, JSON-serializable). Available to the workflow as `github.event.client_payload`.

tools.name: clone-repo
tools.description: Clone a GitHub repository to the local filesystem (uses the current user access token from the Teros GitHub App). Returns {path, branch, sha, recentCommits[]}.

destination.description: Local path where the repo will be cloned (default: /workspace/<repo>)

branch.description: Branch to checkout after cloning (default: default branch)

tools.name: git-status
tools.description: Local git status: branch, ahead/behind vs upstream, and lists of staged, modified, untracked, and conflicted files.

repoPath.description: Absolute path to the cloned repo. If omitted, resolved as `<workspace>/<repo>`.

owner.description: Repository owner (used to resolve default repoPath).

repo.description: Repository name (used to resolve default repoPath).

tools.name: git-add
tools.description: Stage local changes. Pass an array of paths to stage selectively, or omit `paths` (default `.`) to stage everything.

paths.description: Paths relative to repo root. Defaults to ["."] (stage all changes).

update.description: If true, only stage already-tracked files (`git add -u`).

tools.name: git-commit
tools.description: Create a commit with the staged changes. Returns `{ sha, branch, message }`. Use `amend: true` to amend the previous commit instead.

message.description: Commit message (subject + optional body separated by blank line).

amend.description: Amend the previous commit instead of creating a new one.

allowEmpty.description: Allow creating a commit with no staged changes.

author.description: Override commit author (defaults to git config user.name/user.email).

tools.name: git-push
tools.description: Push commits to the remote. `force: true` uses `--force-with-lease`; `forceUnsafe: true` uses raw `--force` (destructive).

branch.description: Local branch to push. Defaults to current branch.

tools.name: git-checkout
tools.description: Switch branches, create a new branch, or restore specific paths. Returns the new HEAD ref. Set `force: true` to discard local changes (destructive).

target.description: Branch, tag, commit SHA, or — with `paths` — restore source.

paths.description: Restore these specific paths from `target` (no branch switch).

tools.name: git-rm
tools.description: Remove tracked files from the working tree and stage the deletion. Pass `cached: true` to only unstage (without deleting from disk).

paths.description: Paths to remove (relative to repo root).

cached.description: Only stage the deletion; keep the file on disk (`git rm --cached`).

tools.name: git-mv
tools.description: Move or rename a tracked file/directory while preserving git history. Both `from` and `to` are relative to repo root.

tools.name: git-read-file
tools.description: Read a file from the working tree or from a specific git revision. Pass `ref` (commit/branch/tag) to read the version at that point.

path.description: File path relative to repo root.

ref.description: Optional commit/branch/tag. If omitted, reads from the current working tree.

encoding.description: Output encoding. Use `base64` for binary files.

tools.name: git-write-file
tools.description: Write file content into the working tree (creates parent dirs) and stage it. Use `stage: false` to skip staging.

path.description: File path relative to repo root.

content.description: File content (utf8 by default, or base64 — see `encoding`).

tools.name: git-list-files
tools.description: List files in the repo, respecting `.gitignore`. Returns `{ tracked, untracked, ignored }` arrays. Optionally filter by `pattern` (glob, relative to repo root).

tools.name: git-pull
tools.description: Pull commits from the remote into the current branch. `rebase: true` for a linear history (no merge commit).

branch.description: Remote branch to pull. Defaults to upstream.

ff.description: `only` = abort if not fast-forward; `no` = always merge commit; `auto` = git default.

tools.name: git-diff
tools.description: Show differences as unified diff + numstat. Defaults to working tree vs HEAD. `from: staged` for index vs HEAD; pass `from`+`to` commit SHAs for arbitrary diffs.

to.description: Target ref when `from` is a commit. Default `HEAD` when `from`=working/staged.

path.description: Limit diff to a specific path.

contextLines.description: Number of context lines around each change.

tools.name: git-log
tools.description: Local commit history with structured entries. Defaults to last 20 commits on the current branch. Filter by `ref`, `path`, `author`, `since`/`until`.

ref.description: Branch / tag / commit to start from (defaults to HEAD).

path.description: Limit history to a specific path.

since.description: ISO date or git-style relative (e.g. "2 weeks ago").

tools.name: git-batch-commit
tools.description: Apply multiple file changes (create/update/delete/rename) and create ONE atomic commit. Use this for refactors and any multi-file change where the intermediate states should not be visible in git history.

tools.name: git-stash
tools.description: Manage the stash. Default action `push` saves uncommitted changes. Other actions: pop, apply, drop, list, clear.

tools.name: git-merge
tools.description: Merge a branch/tag/commit into the current branch. On conflict, throws `GIT_CONFLICT` and the agent should resolve via `git-status` + edit + `git-add`.

message.description: Merge commit message (used when not fast-forward).

squash.description: Squash all changes into a single staged change (does NOT commit).

tools.name: git-rebase
tools.description: Rebase the current branch onto another ref (linear history). Or drive an in-progress rebase with `mode: continue/skip/abort`.

onto.description: Target ref to rebase onto (required unless `mode` is given).

tools.name: git-reset
tools.description: Reset HEAD to `target`. `mode: soft` keeps staging; `mode: mixed` (default) keeps working tree; `mode: hard` discards everything (destructive).

tools.name: git-cherry-pick
tools.description: Cherry-pick commits onto the current branch. Pass `commits: ["sha", ...]` or drive an in-progress pick with `mode: continue/skip/abort`.

noCommit.description: Stage changes but do not create the commit.

mainline.description: For merge commits: parent number (1-indexed) to use as mainline.

tools.name: git-config
tools.description: Read or write git config (whitelisted keys only). Default scope is `local` (the repo). For identity, prefer `user.name` and `user.email`.

tools.name: git-tag
tools.description: List, create, or delete local git tags. Pass `message` on create for an annotated tag (otherwise lightweight).

message.description: If set, create an annotated tag with this message.

tools.name: git-remote
tools.description: List, add, remove, or update git remotes. `list` returns name + fetch/push URLs.

tools.name: git-blame
tools.description: Per-line attribution for a file. Returns `[{ sha, author, date, lineNumber, content }]`. Restrict with `range: "10,50"` or `ref`.

path.description: File path relative to repo root.

ref.description: Blame at a specific ref (default HEAD).

tools.name: git-bisect
tools.description: Binary search for the commit that introduced a bug. Workflow: start → mark each step good/bad → done. Use `reset` to abort.

ref.description: Commit to mark for `good/bad/skip` (default current HEAD).

tools.name: git-fetch
tools.description: Fetch refs from the remote without merging. Use `refspec` to fetch arbitrary refs (e.g. `pull/<n>/head:pr-<n>` for a PR head, `refs/tags/v1.0.0:refs/tags/v1.0.0` for a tag).

refspec.description: Optional refspec — e.g. `pull/<n>/head:pr-<n>` to bring a PR head as a local branch, or `refs/tags/<tag>` to fetch a single tag. If omitted, fetches all branches and tags from the remote.

depth.description: Limit history to N commits (shallow fetch).

tags.description: Also fetch tags (default true for default fetch, false when a refspec is provided).

prune.description: Remove local refs whose remote counterpart is gone (`--prune`).
